summary: A fragment of a first-person novel in which a teenage narrator describes tricking school officials about their records to enter the right grade, viewing school as a prison-like babysitting system, and finding refuge in University of Minnesota libraries. The narrator plans to join a program letting high schoolers take college classes at sixteen, while running a business and a group. The passage ends with Monica commenting on a news photo of Wilson being led out of a house.
one_line: A teen narrator in a novel excerpt escapes dull school life into University of Minnesota libraries while Monica reacts to a news photo of Wilson.
key_facts: The narrator convinced school officials that their records got messed up when they changed schools so they could enter the grade they were supposed to be in.
The narrator says it would have been simpler to read books and take a GED test, but that was not an option.
The narrator describes school as 'a prison system combined with a mass babysitting operation.'
The narrator compares the student body to a can of bargain-bin salted nuts and says classes ran on a 'totally borked class management system.'
After growing taller at fourteen, the narrator started hanging out at the University of Minnesota libraries, which had guest wifi and no screaming little kids.
Google Scholar articles that cost thirty-five bucks are free when accessed from a library computer.
In 2013, Diana finally saw the original 'Garden of Earthly Delights' painting up close after waiting in line for hours.
A college student told the narrator about a program where high school kids can take college classes and get free textbooks.
The narrator planned to apply for the program at sixteen, when eligible.
The narrator was busy running their own business and the Group while keeping up with homework easily.
Monica says 'Wilson's father must be going crazy' while looking at a picture of kids being led out of a house, with Wilson in front.
Wilson looked as if he had just woken up and wondered why people with guns were in his front yard.
